correctness.rationale: Exact averaging/contrast reduction gives F_w(m,d)=(m,phi(d)) with phi(d)=d(1-w(|d|))/(1+w(|d|)). Monotonicity of w ensures phi is odd and increasing; ||phi||Lip<=1 iff H(s)=s*w/(1+w) nondecreasing. Every two-input quotient in coordinate ℓq equals the swap-symmetric matrix A_theta with eigendirections common mean and contrast; induced ℓq norm is max(1,theta). For inverse powers direct differentiation in z=(s/sigma)^p yields derivative peak z=(1+c)(p+1)/(p-1) only if p>1, giving 1+c(p-1)^2/(2p(1+c)); p<=1 sup=1 at infinity only. Gaussian stationary equation 2u(1-v)=3(1+v) has a unique root because the bracket decreases; substitution gives 1+2v(2+v)/(1-v^2). Finite distinct secants cannot equal isolated derivative maxima. Independently recomputed power-law peaks for c=0.1,0.7,1 and p=0.4,1,1.5,3 and Gaussian roots at c=0.1 and 1.

value.rationale: The two-site system is the minimal nontrivial bilateral-filter model and exactly separates one-input smoothing from two-input instability; p=1 is an interpretable tail-decay threshold, with quantitatively sharp worst-case response for standard rational and Gaussian kernels. This precise stability boundary is useful even though it does not generalize automatically to full images.

final_claim: For symmetric two-site bilateral smoothing, two-input path-TV and every coordinate-ℓq nonexpansivity are equivalent to monotonicity of H(s)=s w(s)/(1+w(s)); inverse-power kernels have a sharp p=1 transition with explicit global gain, and Gaussian kernels have a unique sharp amplified derivative maximum.
